ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a unit negative feedback control system. On the left is the summing point where the input and feedback are subtracted, and its output is the error signal E(s). The error signal is divided into two paths: one path enters the proportional element k_p, and the other path enters the integral element k_i/s. The two outputs are summed on the right and then enter the controlled object, whose transfer function is labeled P(s)=ω^2/(s^2+2ξωs+ω^2). The output of the controlled object then returns to the negative terminal of the left summing point in a unit feedback manner. In the figure, z is marked at the output of the integral branch, therefore Z(s)=(k_i/s)E(s). Reasoning: From the unit negative feedback relationship, there is E(s)=R(s)/(1+P(s)C(s)), where C(s)=k_p+k_i/s. The unit step input R(s)=1/s, so Z(s)=(k_i/s)(1/s)/(1+P(s)(k_p+k_i/s)). Since the problem states that the closed loop is stable, the final value theorem can be used: z_ss=lim_{s→0} sZ(s). Substituting gives z_ss=lim_{s→0} k_i/[s(1+P(s)k_p)+P(s)k_i]. The DC gain of the controlled object P(0)=ω^2/ω^2=1, and k_i=10, therefore z_ss=10/(1·10)=1.

method.method_draft: From the image, define P(s)=omega^2/(s^2+2 xi omega s+omega^2), C(s)=k_p+k_i/s, and identify z as the integrator branch output Z(s)=(k_i/s)E(s). Use unity negative feedback to write E(s)=R(s)/(1+P(s)C(s)). For a unit step R(s)=1/s, form Z(s)=(k_i/s)(1/s)/(1+P(s)(k_p+k_i/s)). Since the problem states the closed-loop system is stable, apply the final value theorem: z_ss=lim_{s->0} sZ(s). Evaluate the limit using P(0)=1 and k_i=10 to get z_ss=1.
